extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and dataset/benchmark users working on mathematical problem solving
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, formatting, and evaluating a benchmark dataset (MATH) for mathematical problem solving by ML models, plus an auxiliary pretraining corpus (AMPS). Covers dataset construction, formatting, automatic evaluation, and evaluation protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset size and splits
rubrics_metrics.description: The MATH dataset has 12,500 problems total, with 7,500 training and 5,000 test problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these splits for training and evaluation to enable comparable benchmarking across models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem sources (competition provenance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are drawn from mathematics competitions including the AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more (collected from AoPS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use competition problems to target genuine mathematical problem-solving heuristics rather than plug-and-chug; cite AoPS sources as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects / topical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are tagged by subject: Prealgebra, Algebra, Number Theory, Counting and Probability, Geometry, Intermediate Algebra, and Precalculus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and report performance broken down by these subject categories for fine-grained analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty levels (1–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each problem is assigned a difficulty from '1' to '5', following AoPS: a subject’s easiest problems are level 1 and hardest are level 5 (e.g., early AMC problems are level 1, AIME are level 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report accuracy by difficulty level to analyze model behavior across problem hardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step-by-step solutions included
rubrics_metrics.description: Each problem has a full step-by-step solution written in LaTeX and natural language, plus a final boxed answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions enable training on derivations, provide 'scratch space' supervision, and allow experiments with partial-solution hints and training-on-solutions ablations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting language: LaTeX and Asymptote
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems and solutions are consistently formatted using LaTeX; figures/diagrams are encoded in the Asymptote vector graphics language rather than raster images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables text-only processing of diagrams (models can generate Asymptote) and consistent parseability for automatic evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final answer delimitation (boxed answers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final answers are wrapped and delimited with the \boxed{} command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic assessment parses the contents of \boxed{} to determine the model's final answer location unambiguously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary evaluation metric: exact-match accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Because answers are unique after normalization, MATH is scored with exact match rather than heuristic metrics like BLEU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact-match on the normalized boxed answer as the primary metric for model performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer normalization and equivalence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To allow automatic exact-match evaluation, the dataset applies normalization rules: probabilities expressed as simplified fractions; matrix entry fractions encoded as x/y while other fractions use \frac{x}{y}; coefficients encoded without a multiplication symbol (e.g. 5x not 5*x); expressions with multiple variables in alphabetical order; polynomials in decreasing degree order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating, apply these normalization rules to both ground truth and model output so equivalent expressions are treated identically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted encoding equivalences
rubrics_metrics.description: Different fraction encodings equivalent, such as \frac{x}{y} and \dfrac{x}{y} and x/y; different parenthesis encodings (\left( vs () ) are treated as equivalent; 0.5 and 1/2 (or .1 and 0.1) are treated the same; when answer is factorized polynomial, different orderings of factors are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization must canonicalize these variants (ignore parentheses style, accept equivalent numeric and factor orderings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spaces and units handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces are ignored and units may be included or omitted from an answer (both accepted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should strip whitespace and accept answers with or without unit annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic assessment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic assessment locates the contents of the \boxed{} command and compares that (after applying the formatting/normalization rules) to the ground truth answer to determine exact equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a parser to find \boxed{...} robustly even when models generate full solutions before the final answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of step-by-step solutions at training and inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Two evaluation/training modes: train/evaluate on 'Final Answer' sequences or on 'Full Solution' sequences. Providing partial ground-truth solutions as hints at inference can improve accuracy; training on solutions increases accuracy relative to training on Q/A only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with (1) predicting final answer directly, (2) predicting full solutions then answer, and (3) supplying partial ground-truth steps as hints. Note: generating full solutions before the answer currently degrades accuracy in experiments (hypothesized snowballing effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretraining corpus (AMPS) composition
rubrics_metrics.description: AMPS contains over 100,000 Khan Academy problems with solutions and ~5 million Mathematica-generated problems (23 GB total); 100 hand-designed Mathematica scripts produced ~50k exercises each, 37 of which include step-by-step LaTeX solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMPS is intended for pretraining models on mathematics fundamentals; pretraining on AMPS substantially improves downstream MATH accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMPS pretraining sampling strategy and hyperparameters (guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: During pretraining the authors upsample Khan Academy data by factor 5 and downsample Mathematica by factor 2; pretraining used 1 epoch with AdamW, batch size 128, weight decay 0.05, autoregressive LM objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow similar sampling and optimization settings when reproducing reported pretraining results; these choices affected experimental outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model generation and evaluation hyperparameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Default generation: prompting with 'Problem... Final Answer:' to generate final answer; beam search used with beam size 20 when generating final answers and beam size 10 when generating full solutions; GPT-2 tokenization digit-wise for numbers; evaluate few-shot GPT-3 with temperature 0 and up to 20 tokens for answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing models replicate prompt format and generation/search settings (beam sizes, token limits, temperature) used in the paper for fair comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human baseline measurement protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation: randomly sample 20 MATH test problems, give participants 1 hour to work by hand, require manual calculations; participants were university students with varied math backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use similar constraints (time, hand calculations) for human baselines to make comparisons consistent; report participant backgrounds and scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence and error-detection metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Define confidence as the average prediction probability of tokens in the generated answer. Measure the ability to detect correct vs incorrect answers via AUROC (e.g., GPT-2 1.5B AUROC reported 68.8%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report confidence distributions and AUROC to evaluate calibration and error-detection; note models can be highly overconfident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance reporting by subject and difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Report accuracy broken down across subjects and difficulty levels (e.g., level-1 ~15% accuracy for GPT-2 1.5B, level-5 ~4%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include per-subject and per-difficulty tables/plots to demonstrate where models succeed/fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretraining vs model size interpretation (analysis guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess gains from pretraining (AMPS) relative to parameter scaling; authors report AMPS pretraining can yield similar improvements to a large parameter increase (e.g., 0.1B pretrained on AMPS vs 13B fine-tuned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare pretraining ablations and scaling trends (log-linear fits) to determine whether scaling or algorithmic advances are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended uses and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state they do not intend the dataset to train models that help students cheat on exams; the MATH and AMPS data and code are released under an MIT license; authors assert coverage under Fair Use §107.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the declared intended uses and license when using or redistributing the datasets; document and justify downstream usage consistent with Fair Use and MIT license terms.
